## Dataset

```{r load_data, message=FALSE, include=FALSE}
RT_data <- read_csv(here("05_output", "reading_times2.csv"), col_names=TRUE, id=NULL)
```


```{r total_participants}
length(unique(RT_data$participant_id))
```

## Declare variables
```{r data}
article <- RT_data
```

"As regards very long fixations, deletion (but not merger) is also common. Eye-tracking researchers generally remove fixations longer than 800 ms, as recommended by Conklin and Pellicer-Sánchez (2016) and Keating (2014), because these fixations are believed to signal a lapse in attention." (Godfroid 2020: 261)
```{r outlier, eval=FALSE, include=FALSE}
# Cap the values in the dur column to a maximum of 800
#article$dur <- pmin(article$dur, 800)
```

### Log-Transformation
```{r log_duration}
article <- article %>% mutate(log_dur = log(dur)) # log transform
hist(article$dur)
hist(article$log_dur)
```

**Note:** Values that are *NA* must be dealt with. There are multiple options for handling missing values. 
While they could be removed, this would lead to a loss of data. Another approach is to set it to a very low value, for example 1ms.
```{r dependent_var}
article$dur[is.na(article$dur)] <- 0 
article$log_dur[is.na(article$log_dur)] <- 0

duration = article$dur
log_duration = article$log_dur
```

```{r changes}
article <- article %>% mutate(log_freq = log(frequency))

# additional columns
article <- article %>% mutate(L1 = ifelse(lang == "en", "L1", "L2"))

# Remove stopwords
#article <- article[article$is_stopword != 1, ]

# Remove rows where the AAPz column equals 0
#article <- article[article$AAPz != 0, ]

# Update the AAPz column where is_stopword is 1
#article$AAPz[article$is_stopword == 1] <- 0

# set exposure for EN participants
# article$exposure_EN[article$lang == "en"] <- 100 
```

```{r organize_columns}
article <- article %>% select(textnr, lang, L1, participant_id, 
                              tokenindex, token,

                              dur, log_dur,

                              )
```

## Means and Medians 
#### Mean and Median Duration 
```{r calc_all}
# for illustrative purposes
article %>%
  group_by(token, tokenindex, textnr) %>%
  summarise(mean_dur = round(mean(dur)), median_dur = round(median(dur)), .groups = 'drop')

article <- article %>%
    group_by(token, tokenindex, textnr) %>%
    mutate(mean_dur = mean(dur), median_dur = median(dur), .after=log_dur)
```

#### Median Duration for Language Group
Median duration of each token for each language group.
```{r calc_language}
# for illustrative purposes
article %>%
  group_by(textnr, tokenindex, token, lang) %>%
  summarise(medianDur = median(dur), .groups = 'drop') %>%
  spread(lang, medianDur, sep = "_") %>%
  rename_with(~gsub("^lang_", "median_", .), starts_with("lang_"))

article <- article %>%
  group_by(textnr, token, tokenindex, lang) %>%
  mutate(median_lang = median(dur), .after = median_dur)
```

#### Median Duration for L1 and L2
```{r median_L1L2}
# for illustrative purposes
article %>%
  group_by(textnr, token, tokenindex, L1) %>%
  summarise(valence = first(AAPz), median_dur = median(dur), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = L1, values_from = median_dur)

article <- article %>%
  group_by(textnr, token, tokenindex, L1) %>%
  mutate(median_L1L2 = median(dur), .after = median_dur)
```

## Descriptive Statistics
### Participants
```{r mean_participant}
participant_mean <- article %>% 
  group_by(participant_id) %>% 
  reframe(mean_duration = mean(dur), L1) %>%
  distinct()

cat("Slowest reader: ", 
    participant_mean$participant_id[participant_mean$mean_duration == max(participant_mean$mean_duration)], ",",
    round(max(participant_mean$mean_duration)),"ms", "\n")

cat("Fastest reader: ", 
    participant_mean$participant_id[participant_mean$mean_duration == min(participant_mean$mean_duration)], ",",
    round(min(participant_mean$mean_duration)), "ms")
```


The following density plot shows the mean reading times for each participant split between L1 and L2.
```{r density}
L1L2_mean <- participant_mean %>%
  group_by(L1) %>%
  summarize(L1L2_mean_dur = mean(mean_duration))

ggplot(participant_mean, aes(x = mean_duration, fill = L1)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.75) +
  geom_vline(data=L1L2_mean, aes(xintercept=L1L2_mean_dur, linetype = L1)) +
  labs(title = "Mean Reading Times between L1 and L2",
       x = "Duration",
       y = "Density") +
  scale_fill_grey() +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Skipped Words
```{r percentage_0}
cat("Percentage of 0ms duration (skipped words) using",
    "\n the mean: ",(sum(article$mean_dur==0)/length(article$mean_dur))*100,
    "\n the median: ", round((sum(article$median_dur==0)/length(article$median_dur))*100, 2),
    "\n the median between L1 and L2: ",(round(sum(article$median_L1L2==0)/length(article$median_L1L2)*100, 2)),
    "\n overall: ",round((sum(article$dur==0)/length(article$dur))*100, 2))
```
Median contains a lot of 0 and the mean performs better! 
However, the disadvantage of the mean is that the durations are much higher overall.

```{r percentage_0_by_lang}
article %>%
  group_by(lang) %>%
  summarise(zero_dur = round((sum(dur == 0) / n()) * 100, 2),
            zero_dur_median = round((sum(median_lang == 0) / n()) * 100, 2))
```

```{r plot_1}
ggplot(article, aes(x = lang, y = median_lang, fill = lang)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(title = "Boxplot of Duration by Language",
       x = "Language",
       y = "Duration") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Correlation
```{r cor_matrix}
cor(article[, c("dur", "AAPz", "word_length", "log_freq")])
```

**Note:** This uses the AAPz values. In this case, it must be determined how to deal with stopwords (see above).
```{r correlation}
cat("Correlation with Duration", "\n","Word length:", cor(article$word_length, article$dur), "\n","Word frequency:", cor(article$log_freq, article$dur), "\n","Valence:", cor(article$AAPz, article$dur))
```
```{r correlation_by_language}
article %>%
  group_by(lang) %>%
  summarise(cor_valence=cor(AAPz, dur), cor_length=cor(word_length, dur), cor_frequency=cor(log_freq, dur))
```

```{r correlation_by_L1L2}
part_correlation <- article %>%
  group_by(participant_id) %>%
  mutate(cor_valence=cor(AAPz, dur), cor_length=cor(word_length, dur), cor_frequency=cor(log_freq, dur)) %>%
  group_by(L1) %>%
  mutate(mean_cor_valence = mean(cor_valence)) %>%
  reframe(L1, participant_id, lang, cor_valence, cor_length, cor_frequency, mean_cor_valence) %>% unique()
```

```{r corr_density}
ggplot(part_correlation, aes(x = cor_valence, fill = L1)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.75) +
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept = mean_cor_valence, linetype = L1)) +
  labs(title = "Correlation between Valence and Duration by L1 and L2",
       x = "Correlation",
       y = "Density") +
  scale_fill_grey() +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r boxplot_corr_lang}
ggplot(part_correlation, aes(x = lang, y = cor_valence, fill = lang)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(title = "Boxplot of Correlation between Valence and Duration by Language",
       x = "Language",
       y = "Correlation") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Linear Regression
Multifactorial linear regression analysis. Step-down and step-up analysis, including interactions between variables.
```{r factors}
article$L1 <- factor(article$L1)
article$punctuation <- factor(article$punctuation)
```

### RQ1
```{r RQ1_data}
RQ1_df <- article %>%
  group_by(textnr, token, tokenindex) %>%
  select(textnr, tokenindex, token, mean_dur, median_dur, AAPz, punctuation, word_length, log_freq, is_stopword) %>%
  distinct()
```

```{r RQ1}
model1.1 <- lm(median_dur ~ word_length + (AAPz + I(AAPz^2)) * (log_freq + punctuation), data = RQ1_df)
summary(model1.1)

# without stopwords
model1.2 <- lm(median_dur ~ word_length + (AAPz + I(AAPz^2)) * (log_freq + punctuation), data = RQ1_df[RQ1_df$is_stopword != 1, ])
summary(model1.2)
```

including stopwords is not necessary
```{r anova}
model1.1.2 <- lm(median_dur ~ word_length + (AAPz + I(AAPz^2)) * (log_freq + punctuation) + is_stopword, data = RQ1_df)
anova(model1.1, model1.1.2)
```

```{r residuals_plots}
hist(scale(resid(model1.1)), main = "Histogram of Standardized Residuals", xlab = "Standardized Residuals")
plot(density(scale(resid(model1.1))), main = "Density Plot of Standardized Residuals", xlab = "Standardized Residuals")
qqnorm(scale(resid(model1.1)))
qqline(scale(resid(model1.1)))
```
indicates normal distribution:
- One standard deviation (threshold = 1): This captures approximately 68% of the data.
- Two standard deviations (threshold = 2): This captures approximately 95% of the data.
- Three standard deviations (threshold = 3): This captures approximately 99.7% of the data.

```{r without_outliers}
# remove outliers
model1.3 = lm(median_dur ~ word_length + (AAPz + I(AAPz^2)) * (log_freq + punctuation), 
            data = RQ1_df[abs(scale(resid(model1.1)))<2,])
summary(model1.3)
```

```{r residuals_plot}
# Word length
qplot(word_length, median_dur, data = RQ1_df)

# Valence
qplot(AAPz, median_dur, data = RQ1_df)
qplot(AAPz, median_dur, data = RQ1_df[RQ1_df$is_stopword != 1, ])
qplot(AAPz, median_dur, data = RQ1_df[abs(scale(resid(model1.1)))<2,])

pairs(RQ1_df[,c("median_dur","AAPz","word_length","log_freq")],pch=".")
```


### RQ2
```{r RQ2_df}
RQ2_df <- article %>%
  group_by(textnr, token, tokenindex) %>%
  select(textnr, tokenindex, token, L1, median_lang, lang, AAPz, punctuation, word_length, log_freq, is_stopword) %>%
  distinct()

RQ2_ru = RQ2_df[RQ2_df$lang == 'ru',]
RQ2_he = RQ2_df[RQ2_df$lang == 'he',]
RQ2_fi = RQ2_df[RQ2_df$lang == 'fi',]
```

```{r RQ2, eval=FALSE, include=FALSE}
RQ2.1 <- lm(median_lang ~ word_length + (AAPz + I(AAPz^2)) * (log_freq + punctuation) + is_stopword, data = RQ2_ru)
RQ2.2 <- lm(median_lang ~ word_length + (AAPz + I(AAPz^2)) * (log_freq + punctuation) + is_stopword, data = RQ2_he)
RQ2.3 <- lm(median_lang ~ word_length + (AAPz + I(AAPz^2)) * (log_freq + punctuation) + is_stopword, data = RQ2_fi)

summary(RQ2.1)
summary(RQ2.2)
summary(RQ2.3)

summary(lm(median_lang ~ word_length + (AAPz + I(AAPz^2)) * (log_freq + punctuation) + is_stopword, data = RQ2_ru[abs(scale(resid(RQ2.1)))<2,]))
summary(lm(median_lang ~ word_length + (AAPz + I(AAPz^2)) * (log_freq + punctuation) + is_stopword, data = RQ2_he[abs(scale(resid(RQ2.2)))<2,]))
summary(lm(median_lang ~ word_length + (AAPz + I(AAPz^2)) * (log_freq + punctuation) + is_stopword, data = RQ2_fi[abs(scale(resid(RQ2.3)))<2,]))

```

### RQ3
```{r RQ3_df}
RQ3_df <- article %>%
  group_by(textnr, token, tokenindex) %>%
  select(textnr, tokenindex, token, L1, median_L1L2, AAPz, punctuation, word_length, log_freq, is_stopword) %>%
  distinct()

native = RQ3_df[RQ3_df$L1 == "L1", ]
nonnative = RQ3_df[RQ3_df$L1 == "L2", ]
```

```{r RQ3_models}
summary(lm(median_L1L2 ~ word_length + (AAPz + I(AAPz^2)) * (log_freq + punctuation) + is_stopword, data = native))
summary(lm(median_L1L2 ~ word_length + (AAPz + I(AAPz^2)) * (log_freq + punctuation) + is_stopword, data = nonnative))
```
